attributes.body_ja:
「は元（もと）より」は「(A) だけでなく (B)」や「(A) はもちろん (B) も」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）す文型（ぶんけい）で、ひらがなで書（か）かれることが多（おお）いです。これは「は」と名詞（めいし）「元（もと）」、そして「より」から成（な）り立（た）っており、「もともとの (A) と比（くら）べても (B)」のような比較（ひかく）のニュアンスがあります。多（おお）くの場合（ばあい）、(A) にはその話題（わだい）において明（あき）らかなことや、一般（いっぱん）によく知（し）られている情報（じょうほう）が入（はい）ります。

「はもとより」は名詞（めいし）の後（あと）、または「の」や「こと」で名詞（めいし）化（か）された動詞（どうし）句（く）の後（あと）に置（お）かれます。

また「はもとより」は、(A) が基準（きじゅん）または出発（しゅっぱつ）点（てん）であり、そこからもちろん (B) が成（な）り立（た）つという意味（いみ）を表（あわら）すこともあります。これは前（まえ）に述（の）べた意味（いみ）と似（に）ているように見（み）えますが、この場合（ばあい）の意味（いみ）は「最初（さいしょ）から (A) は (B) だ」や「もともと (A) は (B) だ」のようなものに近（ちか）くなります。どちらの意味（いみ）で使（つか）われているかは、たいてい文（ぶん）の流（なが）れから判断（はんだん）できます。
attributes.body:
は元（もと）より, commonly seen purely in hiragana, is a grammar pattern that indicates 'not only (A), but also (B) ', or 'let alone (A), (B)'. This construction is just a combination of は, the noun 元（もと） 'origin', and より. In this way, it is just highlighting that 'even compared to the original fact of (A), (B)'. Often, (A) will be something that is considered obvious, or the most well known information in regard to the topic.

はもとより may appear after nouns, or verb phrases that have been nominalized with の or こと.

Alternatively, はもとより may be used in structures where it is simply showing that (A) is the base from which (B) is also a fact. Although this may sound similar to the previous meaning, it translates closer to 'from the start, (A) is (B)', or 'by nature, (A) is (B)'. Which meaning is being used will usually be clear in the context of the overall sentence.

attributes.description: 〜に限らず VS 〜のみならず VS 〜はもとより

attributes.body: Both に限らず and はもとより express inclusion beyond an initial example but differ in nuance. に限らず highlights that the mentioned case is not the only one, implying a broader range or scope (not only…but also). はもとより, on the other hand, emphasizes that the stated example is obvious or expected, and contrasts it with less obvious or more significant cases, carrying a nuance closer to 'needless to say…even more so'.

first_relatable.title: に限らず
first_relatable.meaning: Not just, Not only… but also

second_relatable.title: はもとより
second_relatable.meaning: Not only... but also, Let alone, Of course

attributes.body: はもとより and のみならず both mean 'not only... but also'. はもとより is slightly more formal and can add the nuance of 'let alone' for the first part, emphasizing the inclusion of the second. のみならず is still formal but slightly less so, and puts more of the focus on the second thing being a noteworthy addition on top of the first.

first_relatable.title: はもとより
first_relatable.meaning: Not only... but also, Let alone, Of course

second_relatable.title: のみならず
second_relatable.meaning: Not only...but, Not just...but, What is more

attributes.body: はもちろん and はもとより both mean 'not only... but also'. はもちろん adds the nuance of 'of course (A), and also (B)', e.g. 学校はもちろん家でも勉強する ('He studies at home, not just at school'). はもとより is more formal and emphasizes that (A) goes without saying, e.g. 親はもとより先生も反対した ('Not only his parents but also his teacher opposed it').

first_relatable.title: はもちろん
first_relatable.meaning: Not only but also, Let alone, Not to mention, Of course

second_relatable.title: はもとより
second_relatable.meaning: Not only... but also, Let alone, Of course

attributes.body: Both express that something applies to more than one item, but differ in nuance and tone. だけでなく(て)～も is a neutral 'Not only (A), but also (B)', e.g. 日本語だけでなく、韓国語も話せる 'He can speak not only Japanese, but also Korean.' はもとより is more literary and formal, and suggests the first item is obvious, e.g. 親はもとより先生にも感謝しています 'I'm grateful not only to my parents, but also to my teachers.'

first_relatable.title: はもとより
first_relatable.meaning: Not only... but also, Let alone, Of course

second_relatable.title: だけでなく(て)～も
second_relatable.meaning: Not only ~ but ~ also, Not just ~ but ~ also

attributes.body: Both formally express that something applies to more than one item, with different nuance. ばかりでなく is a neutral 'Not only (A), but also (B)', e.g. 日本語ばかりでなく、韓国語も話せる 'He can speak not only Japanese, but also Korean.' はもとより is more literary in tone, and implies that the first item is obvious and the second more noteworthy, e.g. 親はもとより先生にも感謝しています 'I'm grateful not only to my parents, but also to my teachers.'
